title: Slimline scheduler: split runloop, KV-priming agent, and batcher resiliency
creator: Priya Nandakumar
description: Context: our continuous batching controller and global scheduler are sources of tail latency and fragile restart behavior under uneven load. The KV priming logic is embedded inside the scheduler runloop and causes priority inversion when prefetches block admission. This ticket refactors the runloop into a minimal scheduler core + asynchronous KV-priming agent, replaces the global scheduler lock with a per-shard work-stealing queue, and hardens the batcher to gracefully shed low-priority prefetched work during overload. Goals: reduce 99th percentile latency by 20% under bursty traffic, eliminate request stalls caused by synchronous priming, and simplify the shutdown/restart path so swaps and model rollouts complete within SLA windows.
acceptance_criteria: Scheduler core no longer holds the global lock while issuing KV prefetches: validated by code diff and bench that shows <1% time spent in global scheduler lock under synthetic burst test
Prefetch agent runs as a separate async worker and exposes observability metrics (queued_prefetches, prefetch_latency_ms, prefetch_failures) in Console
Batcher accepts high-priority path with unchanged latency and can evict/mark low-priority prefetched sessions when util > 85%
End-to-end benchmark: 99th percentile token latency reduced >=20% on the 'short-chatter-burst' harness compared to baseline runtime-2.3
Rollout plan documented and tested in canary: single-node canary sees no increase in error-rate or tail-latency for 24h
Integration tests for restart/shutdown confirm no KV-cursor leaks and that in-flight sessions are reconciled within configured grace-period
implementation_steps: Create scheduler-core abstraction that exposes enqueue/dequeue and shard affinity APIs
Introduce per-shard work-stealing queue based on ConcurrentDeque (Rust port) and wire to existing admission controller
Extract KV-priming into a standalone async agent with a bounded queue and backpressure signals to admission controller
Add priority tags to prefetch requests and eviction marks to batcher so low-priority sessions are preferred for early eviction
Replace global shutdown path with coordinated drain across scheduler-core and priming-agent; implement grace-period and forced-cutover
Add telemetry: scheduler_lock_time_ms, prefetch_queue_depth, batcher_eviction_count and add logs for forced-eviction events
Write unit and integration tests; make a canary deployment and gather metrics over 24h
Iterate on backpressure thresholds and add an experimental adaptive admission switch guarded by runtime flag
risks: New per-shard queue implementation could underperform on extreme skew leading to less even load distribution
Mistuned eviction policy may increase user-visible partial outputs if low-priority sessions get evicted too eagerly
Instrumentation gaps during rollout could hide edge-case stalls; need thorough canary alerts
decisions: Use per-shard work-stealing over a centralized MPMC queue to reduce global contention
Implement KV-priming as best-effort with no blocking guarantees; admissions see an explicit prefetch_backpressure flag
Keep default eviction policy conservative and expose an opt-in aggressive mode behind feature flag for internal experiments
testing_plan: Unit tests: scheduler-core enqueue/dequeue correctness, work-stealing invariants
Integration: end-to-end traffic replay with production-captured traces (short-chatter-burst and long-stream-mix)
Chaos: kill priming-agent mid-prefetch to validate no persistent KV cursors or double-priming
Load: scale to 3x normal qps and verify eviction path keeps latency within SLO for high-priority traffic
Canary: roll to 5% of cluster nodes for 24h with alerting on prefetch_failures > 1% and 99th latency increase > 10%
notes: Initial microbenchmark: removing priming from scheduler runloop reduced scheduler lock contention from 12% to 2% in a synthetic harness
Prefetch agent should own its own small threadpool to avoid head-of-line blocking in async executor
We will standardize prefetch request metadata so future predictors can signal likely-hot keys to the agent
Follow-up ticket proposed to tie prefetch scoring to runtime Optimize recommendations for quantized models
